Corrected on reconciliation. אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה is rendered by the single English word 'harlot's', so the two morphemes share one unit under rule 30, headed on זוֹנָה as the morpheme carrying the lexeme; the indefinite 'a' belongs to that nominal expression under rule 15 and the English genitive is written inside the token. Rule 30 states the point directly, that such an expression is one unit 'rather than one rendered morpheme beside others marked unrepresented', and adds that what the second morpheme is tagged does not matter, so a full lexical noun fuses on the same terms as a preposition. The subtraction test agrees: dropping 'harlot's' diminishes only the expression as a whole, and no morpheme owns a part of it. The accepted reading marked אִשָּׁה unrepresented beside זוֹנָה, and that split is the competing reading; it is set aside because the chapter fuses on these terms at JER.3.1, 3.6, 3.10 and 3.11, and because the corpus fuses a generic person-noun rather than dropping it at ISA.34.16 and EXO.12.22.

The possessive לְ is left with no English word by the recasting (rules 40, 43).
Suffix takes the English subject pronoun (rule 43).
